contexts: This approach involves the use of speci ﬁ c enzymes, such as DNases or RNases, to selectively degrade the unwanted nucleic acids (Chomczynski and Sacchi, 1987).
However, this method can be time-consuming and may require multiple centrifugation steps to achieve a high degree of purity (Chomczynski and Sacchi, 1987).

In addition, specialized techniques such as density gradient centrifugation can be used to isolate viral particles before nucleic acid extraction, providing a more targeted approach (Chomczynski and Sacchi, 1987).

These kits typically employ silica-based columns or magnetic bead-based technology to bind nucleic acids, followed by washing and elution steps to obtain pure nucleic acid extracts (Chomczynski and Sacchi, 1987).
However, they may require optimization to achieve the desired level of contamination control without adversely affecting the recovery of viral nucleic acids (Chomczynski and Sacchi, 1987).
